Generative AI to quantify uncertainty in weather forecasting
recent_posts.summary: A generative AI model called SEEDS has been developed by Google to efficiently generate ensembles of weather forecasts, quantifying the uncertainty in weather conditions. This technology provides a cost-effective solution compared to traditional physics-based forecasting models. SEEDS leverages generative AI to produce real-weather-like forecasts that match or exceed physics-based ensembles. It allows for the generation of large ensembles to accurately assess rare but high-impact weather events.

recent_posts.title: AutoBNN: Probabilistic time series forecasting with compositional bayesian neural networks
recent_posts.summary: AutoBNN is an open-source package that automates the discovery of interpretable time series forecasting models while providing high-quality uncertainty estimates. By combining traditional probabilistic approaches with neural networks, AutoBNN brings scalability and flexibility to time series forecasting.

recent_posts.title: Computer-aided diagnosis for lung cancer screening
recent_posts.summary: Lung cancer is a leading cause of cancer-related deaths and late diagnosis reduces survival chances. Google has developed machine learning models for lung cancer detection and has studied how these models can effectively communicate findings to radiologists. The models have shown high performance and have been evaluated in reader studies. The studies have demonstrated that the models improve clinician performance and can potentially reduce unnecessary follow-up procedures.

recent_posts.title: Using AI to expand global access to reliable flood forecasts
recent_posts.summary: Floods are a common natural disaster that cause significant financial damages. Upgrading early warning systems for accurate and timely information can save lives. AI-based technologies have improved global flood forecasts and extended reliability from zero to five days.

recent_posts.title: ScreenAI: A visual language model for UI and visually-situated language understanding
recent_posts.summary: ScreenAI is a visual language model for UI and visually-situated language understanding. It improves upon previous models with a flexible patching strategy, achieving state-of-the-art results on various tasks. The model is trained using a unique mixture of datasets and tasks, and performs well on benchmarks compared to models of similar size. The study concludes that further research is needed to bridge the gap with larger models.

recent_posts.title: SCIN: A new resource for representative dermatology images
recent_posts.summary: A new dataset called SCIN has been released to address the limitations of existing dermatology image datasets. It contains over 10,000 images of diverse skin conditions, including rashes, allergies, and infections, across various skin tones and body parts. The dataset aims to ensure that future AI tools work effectively for all.

recent_posts.title: MELON: Reconstructing 3D objects from images with unknown poses
recent_posts.summary: A technique called MELON is presented in this post, which can determine object-centric camera poses and reconstruct 3D objects without the need for approximate pose initializations, complex GAN training schemes, or pre-training on labeled data.

recent_posts.title: HEAL: A framework for health equity assessment of machine learning performance
recent_posts.summary: The HEAL framework proposes a methodology to assess whether ML-based health technologies perform equitably by measuring their performance with respect to health disparities. A case study on a dermatology model reveals potential improvements for non-cancer conditions across age. The HEAL framework provides a useful evaluation framework during model development and in real-world monitoring stages.

recent_posts.title: Cappy: Outperforming and boosting large multi-task language models with a small scorer
recent_posts.summary: Cappy is a small scorer that boosts the performance of large multi-task language models. It functions either independently on classification tasks or as an auxiliary component for generation tasks. Cappy can adapt multi-task LLMs without requiring back-propagation through LLM parameters, reducing memory requirements. It outperforms other LLMs and achieves parameter efficiency.
